items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: PCRS Respiratory Conference 2026, Telford International Centre, 24 to 26 September
items.summary: The Primary Care Respiratory Society holds its annual conference at the Telford International Centre from 24 to 26 September 2026. The main UK primary care respiratory gathering, and a route to primary care prescribers and respiratory leads.

items.title: ResMed wins £9.8m, 5-year framework deal to supply Leeds Teaching Hospitals' non-invasive respiratory equipment
items.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust has awarded ResMed a single-supplier contract worth £9,798,912 (inc. VAT) to supply non-invasive ventilation and high-flow therapy devices, consumables and associated services for five years.

items.title: Trafford General performs UK's 100th Inspire sleep apnoea implant
items.summary: ENT surgeons at Trafford General Hospital (Manchester University NHS FT) carried out the 100th UK procedure for the Inspire hypoglossal nerve stimulation implant for moderate-to-severe OSA in CPAP-intolerant patients.

items.title: Semaglutide linked to 40% reduction in asthma attacks
items.summary: Weight loss and diabetes treatment semaglutide is associated with a nearly 40% reduction in asthma attacks among people with the condition, according to new analysis.

items.title: Many GPs cannot access key asthma test for children
items.summary: GPs across large parts of the country cannot access a key, NICE-recommended test for diagnosing asthma in children, a charity has warned.

items.title: Sleep app supports earlier detection of respiratory illness, finds study
items.summary: A smartphone app which collects data on coughing during sleep could help detect respiratory illness and signal outbreaks early, according to a new study by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). The UKHSA said data suggests the app could provide a one-week early warning of flu and Covid-19.
